title: High-throughput Synthesis of Carbohydrates and Functionalization of Polyanhydride Nanoparticles
protocol: Prepare a suitably protected sugar donor and acceptor on the bench-top.
Write a program for the automated synthesis of dimannoside.
Ensure that before adding the promoter, the mixture of donor and acceptor is stirred for at least 30 minutes.
Make solutions of synthetic donor, acceptor, and trimethylsilyltrifluoromethanesulfonate in dichloromethane.
Prepare solutions of reagents for deprotection in 80% methanol and 100% methanol.
Ensure the relative humidity in the automation chamber is 30% or lower before starting the program.
Transfer solutions of donor and acceptor into the reaction vial sequentially using a robotic arm.
Stir the mixture for 30 minutes.
Add 0.2 to 0.3 equivalents of trimethylsilyltrifluoromethanesulfonate into the mixture.
Stir the reaction mixture for an additional 30 minutes.
Stop the reaction after 30 minutes.
Remove a small aliquot to monitor the reaction progress.
Continue the reaction if incomplete until completion.
Transfer the complete reaction mixture to FSPE cartridges containing C8F17-modified silica gel.
Wash the cartridges with an 80% methanol-water mixture (8 mL).
Wash the cartridges with 100% methanol to obtain the fluorous-tagged product.
Purify the product by additional means if required.
Dispense sodium methoxide into the reaction vial using the robotic arm.
Stir the reaction for 2 hours.
Continue stirring until complete if incomplete after 2 hours.
After completion, purify the product by FSPE.
Dissolve the purified product in anhydrous toluene.
Evaporate to remove residual water.
Repeat steps from stopping the reaction to evaporation until the desired chain length is obtained.
Purify the protected product using techniques such as nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) spectroscopy.
Complete deprotection of the final target molecule outside the automation platform.
Carry out ozonolysis of the double bond in fluorous tag.
Oxidize the produced aldehyde to a carboxylic acid.
Purify the product by column chromatography.
Deprotect benzyl ether groups by palladium-catalyzed hydrogenation.
Pass the product through a celite pad to remove palladium.
Synthesize high-throughput polymers and fabricate nanoparticles following a specific protocol.
Use copolymer systems based on sebacic acid (SA), 1,6-bis(para-carboxyphenoxy)hexane (CPH), and 1,8-bis(para-carboxyphenoxy)-3,6-dioxaoctane (CPTEG) for particle fabrication.
Attach the holder containing tubes with the nanoparticle library back to the linear actuator stage.
Mix 10 equivalents of EDC and 10 equivalents of ethylenediamine in an aqueous solution.
Load 12 equivalents of NHS in aqueous solution into a syringe.
Deposit reagent suspensions into the nanoparticle library using LabVIEW program.
Sonicate each sample for 30 seconds at 40 Hz.
Incubate nanoparticle suspensions with constant rotation at 4°C for 9 hours.
Centrifuge tubes at 12,000 x g for 5 minutes.
Perform two washing steps on the centrifuged nanoparticles.
For washing, load an empty syringe in the first programmable syringe pump and fill the second pump with cold water.
Withdraw supernatant from each tube into the empty syringe using the first pump.
Deposit cold water into the tubes using the second pump.
Centrifuge the tubes at 12000 x g for 5 min.
Repeat the wash step as described previously.
Load 12 eq. of EDC with one pump and 12 eq. of NHS with the second pump for the first deposition step.
For the second deposition step, load 10 eq. of specific saccharide on both the first and second pumps.
Load 10 eq. of glycolic acid in a third pump as control.
Homogenize nanoparticle suspension as described previously.
Incubate the nanoparticles with constant rotation at 4 °C for 9 hours.
Perform wash step as described previously after incubation.
Place functionalized nanoparticle library in a vacuum chamber to dry for at least 2 hours.
Characterize functionalized nanoparticles by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy to determine surface composition.
Determine the concentration of saccharide on the surface using a high throughput phenol-sulfuric acid assay.
Utilize scanning electron microscopy to measure particle size and size distribution.
Use dynamic light scattering to assess surface charge.
Synthesize the fully protected dimannoside using an automation platform.
Characterize the synthesized compound by 1H NMR in a VXR 400 MHz spectrometer using CDCl3 as solvent.
Carry out the reaction at 4°C instead of room temperature to reduce nanoparticle aggregation.
Optimize reaction conditions (temperature and time) for nanoparticle functionalization and morphology.
Functionalize polyanhydride nanoparticles with dimannose, lactose, or galactose under optimal conditions.
